findings.title: New installation records bypass the GitHub installer identity check
findings.body: When no `Integration` record exists yet, this returns `pipeline.next_step()` before checking the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user. The subsequent `build_integration` call obtains installation details but does not obtain or persist the installer identity. GitHub webhook delivery that creates the Integration can be delayed or fail, so an attacker who supplies another installation ID during that window can complete the flow after authorizing their own GitHub account and attach that installation to their Sentry organization. The flow must fail closed until an installer identity from a trusted installation webhook is available, or otherwise validate the installer before creating the integration.

findings.title: Installer comparison crashes for integrations without webhook sender metadata
findings.body: This direct indexing assumes every active Integration has `metadata['sender']['login']`, but integrations created by this pipeline do not set `sender`: `OAuthLoginView` only stores `github_authenticated_user`, and `build_integration` only copies `state['sender']` when it exists even though no view binds that state. The existing basic-flow test also expects metadata without `sender`. Any later install/reinstall attempt that reaches this branch for such an integration (including pre-existing integrations) raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 rather than the intended installation error. Handle missing sender metadata explicitly and fail safely (or ensure it is persisted before this branch is reachable).
